cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus, is carrying the good news from city to city. Now he leaves Athens and goes to Corinth, where he finds a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, and his wife Priscilla. They've just come from Italy, and trust me, friend, they did NOT leave Rome for a vacation.

cards.question: Why did Aquila and Priscilla have to leave Rome?

answers.text: The emperor Claudius ordered all Jews out
A great famine struck the whole city
A fire burned their whole street down

cards.text: Paul goes to visit them, and he ends up staying and working with them. Friend, if I found another stamper out here, I would NOT be visiting. My mustache would be on the good side of the counter before he finished saying hello.

cards.question: Paul stays and works with Aquila and Priscilla because they're ___ by trade, just as he is.

cards.text: So Paul's got a day job now. But every Sabbath, he's in the synagogue, reasoning and trying to persuade.

cards.question: Every Sabbath in the synagogue, Paul tries to persuade only the Jews.

cards.text: Then Silas and Timothy, Paul's traveling partners, come down from Macedonia. The whole crew's back together, and now Paul devotes himself fully to the word.

cards.question: Now Paul testifies to the Jews that Jesus is ___.

cards.text: But they oppose him and insult him. So Paul shakes out his garments and tells them, "Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it."

cards.question: After the insults, who does Paul say he'll go to from now on?
So Paul walks out of the synagogue. Where does he go?

cards.text: Titus Justus, a worshiper of God, lives NEXT DOOR to the synagogue. That's like quitting your job and setting up your desk in the company parking lot.
Now, the leader of that synagogue is a man named Crispus. I bet the whole synagogue is holding its breath on this one.

cards.question: Crispus, the synagogue leader, believes in the Lord, along with his whole household.
And many of the Corinthians who hear the message believe and are ___.

cards.text: Paul's been opposed and insulted in this city. Then one night, the Lord speaks to him in a vision.

cards.question: In the vision, the Lord tells Paul not to be ___, but to keep on speaking and not be silent.
The Lord says He is with Paul, and no one will lay a hand on him, because He has many ___ in this city.
So Paul stays in Corinth, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians. For how long?

cards.text: A YEAR AND A HALF of teaching. Then, while Gallio is proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinate an attack on Paul.

cards.question: Where do the Jews who attack Paul bring him?

cards.text: "This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law," they say. Paul's ready, mouth open, first word loading.

cards.question: Paul gets to make his defense before Gallio.

cards.text: Just as Paul is about to speak, Gallio cuts in. He tells the Jews that if this were a wrongdoing or vicious crime, it would be reasonable to hear their complaint.

cards.question: Gallio says this isn't a crime. What does he call it instead?

answers.text: A dispute about words and their own law
A quarrel over who owns the synagogue
A fight between two families over land

cards.question: Gallio agrees to judge the case himself.

cards.text: And Gallio drives them away from the judgment seat. Paul never got a single word in, and the case STILL went his way.

cards.question: Then the crowd seizes a man and beats him right in front of the judgment seat. Who is it?
Gallio steps in to stop the crowd from beating Sosthenes.

findings.problem: Paul being an apostle of Jesus and carrying the good news from city to city are not stated in Acts 18:1-2. These outside facts are given without a supporting reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: No earlier card identifies the shared trade or gives a clue from which to infer it. A baker using only the earlier cards must choose tentmakers, fishermen or potters by luck or prior knowledge, so the blank tests wording they have not seen rather than meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The opening sentence, "So Paul's got a day job now," uses Paul's work from Acts 18:3, but the card cites only Acts 18:4.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Calling Silas and Timothy Paul's traveling partners and saying the whole crew is back together depend on their earlier travels and separation, which are not stated in Acts 18:5. No reference is supplied for that outside context.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The statement that Paul has been opposed and insulted in Corinth retells Acts 18:6, but the card cites only Acts 18:9.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The standalone question does not identify the matter before Gallio. "This" and "it" point back to the accusation and legal proceeding on earlier cards that are no longer visible; the question should supply that context itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The statement that Paul never got a word in uses Acts 18:14, and the statement about the case's outcome also draws on Acts 18:15. Citing only Acts 18:16 does not cover everything the card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
